learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of References and Montages.
Apply References and Montages to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: EEG channels display one electrode relative to another or to a calculated reference. Changing the montage changes the appearance, not the underlying recording.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Bipolar, referential and average-reference montages answer different questions. Phase reversal, field distribution and common-reference contamination must be understood before localisation.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Montage switching is essential for distinguishing true fields from reference artifacts and for localising epileptiform activity.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Reading only one montage can hide or manufacture apparent abnormalities.

quizBank.question: Which statement best captures References and Montages?
options: EEG channels display one electrode relative to another or to a calculated reference. Changing the montage changes the appearance, not the underlying recording.
It provides a stand-alone psychiatric diagnosis
It is unaffected by state and artifact
Its interpretation requires no clinical context
quizBank.explanation: EEG channels display one electrode relative to another or to a calculated reference. Changing the montage changes the appearance, not the underlying recording.

quizBank.question: What is the safest clinical principle for References and Montages?
options: Integrate raw signal quality, state, method and clinical context
Assume a coloured map shows exact anatomy
Treat statistical rarity as proof of disorder
quizBank.explanation: EEG and QEEG interpretation requires converging evidence, technical validity and clinical context.

quizBank.question: Which error is most important to avoid in References and Montages?
options: Reading only one montage can hide or manufacture apparent abnormalities.
quizBank.explanation: Reading only one montage can hide or manufacture apparent abnormalities.

reviewPrompts.answer: Bipolar, referential and average-reference montages answer different questions. Phase reversal, field distribution and common-reference contamination must be understood before localisation.
Montage switching is essential for distinguishing true fields from reference artifacts and for localising epileptiform activity.
Reading only one montage can hide or manufacture apparent abnormalities.
Never interpret a waveform without knowing what is being subtracted from what.
